disclaimer: Reminder reference only — NOT legal authority. Season dates, zones, and limits are set annually and can change. Always verify current regulations with Colorado Parks and Wildlife before hunting or trapping.

license_summary.furbearer_license: A Colorado furbearer license is required to hunt or trap furbearers. Consult the CPW small game/furbearer guide for license types and fees.
license_summary.method_warning: Recreational and commercial leghold traps, instant-kill body-gripping traps, snares, and poisons are generally prohibited in Colorado; live cage/box traps remain available, with narrow statutory exceptions (e.g., 30-day exemptions). Check CPW for the current lawful methods.

sources.notes: Adopted by the Parks and Wildlife Commission July 16, 2026; effective September 1, 2026. Season dates, daily limits, and the beaver sealing requirement read directly from this rule. Archived locally in hidden_files/season-research/.

verification.confirmation_notes: Chapter W-3 as approved July 16, 2026 and effective September 1, 2026 — the current rule for the 2026–27 season — verified 2026-09-18. All 17 furbearers' seasons and daily limits read directly from the rule. River otter and Canada lynx have no open season in the furbearer chapter; lynx is state- and federally endangered (CPW), and otters are a protected restored population (CPW 'Year of the Otter,' 2026).
known_gaps: Scientific names are standard taxonomy, NOT stated in Chapter W-3 — all flagged scientific_name_verified=false.
Kit fox is not addressed in the Chapter W-3 open-season list; it is not modeled. If CPW lists it as protected elsewhere, a closed entry may need to be added.
Beaver and bobcat mandatory sealing/check requirements exist in the rule but CPW sealing locations/deadlines are not modeled — users must check CPW.
Detailed lawful-method rules (cage-trap specifications, statutory exemptions) are not modeled — only the major prohibition warning is included.
No zone structure: all open species are statewide in the rule.
